source.section: Pub OR-17 PDF p.82 'Railroad Retirement Board benefits' (subtraction code 330); Form OR-40 line 11 and Pub OR-17 PDF p.83 'Social Security benefits'; Form OR-40 lines 7-19, 20, 24-25, 27-29 (PDF p.3-4); instructions PDF p.16 line 17 and Table 5, PDF p.16-17 line 20 and tax tables, PDF p.32 Chart S and Chart J, PDF p.17-18 line 25 and Exemption credit worksheet; Pub OR-17 PDF p.143 marginal rates

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = railroad retirement (Tier 2) annuity (person 0) 15,000.00 + private pension (person 1) 30,010.00 + taxable Social Security 17,058.50 = 62,068.50. Social Security gross 24,000.00, federal taxable part 17,058.50 by the federal worksheet. Federal taxable income = 62,068.50 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 2 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = 27,368.50 (the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form OR-40 (filing status married filing jointly): line 7 federal AGI 62,068.50. Line 8 additions (Schedule OR-ASC line A5): other-state bond interest, code 158, 0.00. Line 9 = 62,068.50 + 0.00 = 62,068.50. Line 10 federal tax liability subtraction: the projection leaves it out (not_modelled), 0.00 here; the return subtracts the smaller of the federal tax and the Table 4 maximum, up to 8,500 (4,250 separate). Line 11 Social Security in federal AGI 17,058.50. Line 12 Oregon refund 0.00. Line 13 Schedule OR-ASC line B7: railroad retirement, code 330, 15,000.00. Line 14 = 0.00 + 17,058.50 + 0.00 + 15,000.00 = 32,058.50. Line 15 = 62,068.50 - 32,058.50 = 30,010.00. Line 16 itemized 0.00. Line 17 standard deduction 5,670.00 + 2 age 65 box(es) x 1,000.00 = 7,670.00. Line 18 = 7,670.00. Line 19 = 30,010.00 - 7,670.00 = 22,340.00. Line 20: 8,800.00 x 4.75% = 418 + 13,400.00 x 6.75% = 904.5 + 140.00 x 8.75% = 12.25; total 1334.75, to the cent 1,334.75 (the tax table's J column, row 22,300 to 22,400, gives 1,336; expected keeps the formula). Lines 21-23 0.00. Line 24 = 1,334.75. Line 25 exemption credit: federal AGI 62,068.50 is not more than 200,000.00; 2 x 256.00 = 512.00. Line 27 retirement income credit (code 811) worksheet: line 3 retirement income of the eligible individual(s) 30,010.00; line 4 15,000.00; line 5 Social Security and railroad 39,000.00; line 6 0.00; line 7 household income = 62,068.50 - 17,058.50 + 0.00 = 45,010.00; line 8 30,000.00; line 9 15,010.00; line 10 = 0.00; line 11 0.00; credit 0.00. Line 28 credits = 512.00 + 0.00 = 512.00. Line 29 and line 31 state income tax = 1,334.75 - 512.00 = 822.75. Code 351 medical subtraction: no medical expenses in the inputs, not modelled. Line 32 kicker comes after this figure and is not applied (not_modelled).
accepted_approximations: The federal tax liability subtraction is not applied (not_modelled). This is the largest gap for most Oregon households.
Tax is figured on the exact income; under 50,000 of taxable income the booklet taxes each table row at its middle and rounds, and the Department rounds at each bracket edge.
